input: Could outside workshops alone handle 1,500 beanies within two weeks?

answers:
Yes — outside workshops alone can cover 1,500 accessories (beanies) within two weeks. The cheapest plan starts 1 April and completes 14 April 2026, inside the 14-day window, at 1,820 in external processing charges.

| Workshop | Pieces | Ready |
|---|---|---|
| W6 Nimble Needle | 1,300 | 2026-04-14 |
| W2 SteadyHands | 200 | 2026-04-06 |

Risk is **Medium**: 92% chance every batch comes back clean. W2 SteadyHands (200 pieces) is low risk — 3% rework chance, "never early, never late, never sloppy"; even a rework would land by 10 April. The exposure is W6 Nimble Needle (1,300 pieces): 5% rework chance, and a full redo could arrive as late as 26 April — after the deadline. That rework time isn't in the data, so real delays would be shorter.

In-house was excluded (its cost isn't in the data), and these are external per-piece charges only — transport and rework are not included; currency is unspecified. Source: workshops.csv rows W6 and W2. Worth noting this is a new-batch scenario, not a forecast for any existing order — and a later deadline or an explicit allocation away from W6 would reduce risk; want me to price that alternative?
